summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 69 of CipherBox (porting the node/v3 model to the Rust FUSE/WinFsp desktop stack with grant-root awareness), using the GSD plan-phase and execute-phase workflows end-to-end, including auto-advancing from planning into execution.
summary.outcome: Planned and merged 19/20 non-Windows plans (core+sdk node/v3 foundation, the atomic FUSE cutover, JournalOp reshape, grant-scoped delete/rename gate, recycle-bin and vault-creation migrations, legacy-type deletion), all workspace-green with full test suites passing. User then flagged that desktop-e2e couldn't meaningfully run because desktop root-key recovery was still a legacy v2/placeholder bridge, so 5 more plans (69-21..25) were researched and authored (not yet executed) to port the web's real vault-blob-v3 model before the phase can be called complete; 69-14 (WinFsp) remains deferred to the user's Windows machine.

repo: gsd's git commit helper frequently reports 'commit_failed' as a false negative even when the commit lands cleanly — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.

Worktree-isolated gsd-executor agents mis-report `expected_base` in `<worktree_metadata>` as their own last docs commit rather than the true fork base — always verify via `git merge-base <branch> HEAD` before recording/merging.

Running `cargo fmt` on a crate-root `lib.rs` recursively reformats the entire module tree, introducing out-of-scope diffs; executors must `git checkout --` unrelated reformatted files before committing.
Fresh worktrees lack `node_modules`, so husky pre-commit `lint-staged` fails on first commit; fix via `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` or `--no-verify` when the change is pure Rust.
D-07 dual-keying convention: `SealedChildRef` (read plane) is keyed by `ipnsName`; `WriteChildRef` (write plane) is keyed by the node's `childId` UUID (`uuid_from_ino`). Never conflate the two.
Terminal-owner zeroization is enforced by the type system: `parent_read_key`/`parent_write_key` are passed as borrows (`&[u8]`), so callers can never accidentally zero a caller-owned buffer.

SC#6 (single gated read entrypoint) is enforced via a CI grep gate for raw `resolve_ipns_verified`/`resolve_published_node` calls in `crates/fuse/src`, with `// sc6-allow:` markers for sanctioned exceptions (bin subsystem, file-meta-reencrypt, replay).

`RotationHighWater<S>` is not `Clone` by default even though its `JsonSidecarFloorStore` only wraps a `PathBuf` doing read-modify-write on disk — safe to add `#[derive(Clone)]` since clones share the same durable floor file.

`ApiNodeFetcher` is a lifetime-bound borrow adapter (`struct ApiNodeFetcher<'a> { api: &'a ApiClient }`) with no `::new` constructor — must be constructed inline at each call site, not stored as a struct field (would be self-referential).

Legacy folder-model types (`FolderMetadata`, `FilePointer`, `FolderEntry`, `FileMetadata`) were NOT dead code even after the FUSE flip — they remained load-bearing for the recycle-bin subsystem, vault-export/decrypt helpers, and vault-creation, none of which were in the original migration scope.

The web side already shipped the real node/v3 root-key model in #578: vault blob v3 stores two independent random 32-byte keys (`rootReadKey`/`rootWriteKey`) ECIES-wrapped under the user key, with the root Ed25519 IPNS keypair HKDF-derived separately. The Rust desktop was still on the legacy single-key v2 blob, making web-created and desktop-created vaults mutually unreadable.

A frozen cross-language KAT vector `tests/vectors/vault-v3-blob.json` already existed waiting for a Rust port of the vault-blob-v3 codec — confirms format parity work should always check for pre-existing KAT vectors before designing from scratch.

code.finding: Comment explicitly documents the placeholder key bridge: 'Until that recovery is wired, we bridge from the legacy root_folder_key' — the root cause of desktop-e2e being unreachable.
Mount-consistent bridge key derivation: root_read_key = root_folder_key[..32], root_write_key = root_read_key XOR 0xA5 — a placeholder that must be replaced by real vault-blob-v3 recovery.
list_folder_owned entrypoint signature recovers per-node {read_key, write_key, ipns_private_key} through the shared SC#6 gate for FUSE write-owner materialization.

Original research cited a JournalOp.parent_metadata: FolderMetadata weld here as a key blocker; on later re-verification this field did not exist in the live tree — a stale research finding that nearly drove an incorrect plan.

InodeKind::{Root,Folder,File} store ipns_private_key plus folder_key/file_key — confirming the FUSE mount is a read-WRITE vault owner, not a read-only client like the web 68.2 mirror, which blocked a simpler read-path-only migration.

workflow: For large atomic architectural cutovers that can't reach a compiling intermediate state, break the grind into bounded per-session 'slices' on one shared worktree branch, each committing atomically with RED-elsewhere expected, and record carry-forward facts in a durable runbook file so the grind survives session/usage-limit interruptions.

When an executor halts with an architectural blocker, independently re-verify its central claims (grep counts, blast radius) before accepting or escalating — subagents can be either overcautious or accurately grounded, and this must be checked rather than assumed.

When a plan's boundary is 'the crate is red until the whole flip lands,' gate the final merge on live integration/e2e tests rather than compile-green alone — compile-green does not prove crypto correctness for a security-sensitive migration.

Prefer deleting legacy-model unit tests wholesale (rather than blind-porting ~200 of them) when the model they assert no longer exists, and instead rely on a live E2E gate for deep crypto correctness — matches this repo's established split of crypto correctness (SDK unit tests) vs FUSE mechanics (E2E).

friction: gsd-planner crashed mid-run twice from API errors (connection closed / response stalled mid-stream), requiring filesystem-fallback recovery of partially-written plans.
Hit the account session limit twice mid-execution ('resets 2pm Berlin', later 'resets 7pm Berlin'), stalling the executor grind until reset.

Three successive architectural blockers were discovered only during execution despite upfront research and planning passes — the FUSE read/write coupling, the missing Node write-plane emit API, and the missing write-owner materialization API — each requiring a new research→plan→approve cycle.
cargo fmt repeatedly reformatted unrelated files across nearly every executor run due to crate-root lib.rs rustfmt behavior, requiring manual scope verification and reverts before each commit.
A durable handoff scratchpad path was mistakenly written with a doubled 'phase69' segment and had to be corrected mid-session.

Discovered late in the grind (Slice 5) that the crate's test-compile boundary was ~250+ errors, far larger than the runbook's 'mechanical field-repointing' estimate — required an explicit re-scope and test-deletion strategy decision.

After declaring 19/20 plans complete and workspace-green, the user identified that desktop-e2e was structurally unreachable because desktop root-key recovery was still a legacy placeholder bridge — a completeness gap not caught by any of the prior gates (cargo check, unit tests, plan-checker).
open_items: 69-14 (WinFsp/Windows integration + TEST-03) remains deferred to the user's own Windows machine — autonomous:false, never executed in this session.
ROT-07 live-wiring gap: shared-scope-exit deletes/moves fail closed (EIO) on Unix because no production RotationDeps implementor exists yet; private deletes are correct.

Plans 69-21 through 69-25 (Rust port of vault-blob-v3 root-key model, KeyState two-key fields, desktop init/recovery, mount wiring removing the 0xA5 bridge, and the desktop-e2e verifier fix) were authored and committed but not yet executed.
The actual desktop-e2e run (native local stack: Postgres/api/Kubo/Redis/mock-ipns-routing + FUSE-T) has not yet been performed — it is the real completion gate once 69-21..25 land.
File `versions` are not reconstructed on write in the new node/v3 model (InodeKind dropped `versions`) — flagged as a versioning regression to verify at E2E.
Orphaned parent-CID pins after replay re-publish are not unpinned (GC-able, not correctness-critical) — flagged but not addressed.

Windows platform-layer edits (`platform/windows/*.rs`) were made best-effort during each slice but are unverified locally (macOS can't compile windows-only crates); the Windows CI job / 69-14 is the authoritative check.

`crates/core::folder::VersionEntry` and the `folder` module were intentionally retained (not deleted) because `crates/fuse/src/helpers.rs` still consumes it — a deliberate scope narrowing from the original 'delete all legacy types' plan.
